title: CharacterBody2D.is_on_wall() triggers on one-way platforms for capsule/round collider shape
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in: 4.3, v4.4.beta3.official [06acfccf8]

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta3 - Fedora Linux 41 (KDE Plasma) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (nvidia; 565.77) - AMD Ryzen 7 7700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

When using one-way platforms, for example as part of a TileMapLayer, then is_on_wall() will trigger for CollisionShape2D with CapsuleShape2D or CircleShape2D when hitting a top corner of a tile with the bottom side of the character. If implementing wall jumping/sliding this leads to the character getting stuck inside one-way platforms consisting of multiple tiles.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc2c625d-5b04-4545-8113-8bcc0be2f79c)

Shape is triggering is_on_wall against the tile to the left of it.

*Update:* Just tested, and it happens with a StaticBody2D+CollisionShape2D set to one_way_collision=true too.

### Steps to reproduce

In MRP, jump through the platforms (all tiles are one-way platforms) until you hit a corner at the right angle. The character is drawn in red whenever is_on_wall() is true.

The CharacterBody2D has an exported bool to switch it to use a RectangleShape2D instead (visibility and active collider is updated automatically in _ready). Observe that is_on_wall() never becomes true for this shape.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[capsule_collider_wall_jump.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18809507/capsule_collider_wall_jump.zip)
